# OpenOrbia

> OpenOrbia lists free AI tools for small businesses, job seekers and security teams: open source, or a real free plan with no trial and no card. Each tool's free tier, card requirement, data location, setup, paid parts and biggest catch are checked against its official docs, with the date shown.

- No ads. No paid placement. No affiliate links. A tool never pays to be listed.
- We check every tool's activity and license every month, and recheck the full Free facts at least every 3 months. Each card shows its last-checked date.
- "Not confirmed" means the official docs did not say; it is not a yes or a no.
- Our checks cover the license, pricing, setup and where your data goes, read from each tool's official docs. They are not a security audit: we don't review a tool's code or dependencies for vulnerabilities or malware. Before you run a tool, especially one that installs with a script, downloads programs or model files, or scans and attacks systems, review it yourself and try it somewhere isolated first.
- Tools are "Docs checked" unless marked "Hands-on tested", which OpenOrbia gives only to tools it has actually run.
- Each tool page is the source of truth for its facts: https://openorbia.com/tool/<slug>/. Every fact for every tool is in https://openorbia.com/llms-full.txt.

## Small businesses

- [AnythingLLM](https://openorbia.com/tool/anythingllm/): Chat with your business documents in an AI app. Desktop or server; works with local models. License: MIT. Setup: Desktop app. Free tier: Free desktop app or self-hosted Docker (MIT); paid hosted option. The catch: Multi-user and embed widget need the Docker version; local AI needs decent hardware (works with local AI)
- [Ollama](https://openorbia.com/tool/ollama/): Run open AI models on your own computer or server. License: MIT. Setup: Desktop app. Free tier: Free & unlimited for local models (MIT); paid cloud optional. The catch: Local models run on your own hardware; cloud models are billed per token on pay as you go (works with local AI)
- [n8n](https://openorbia.com/tool/n8n/): Automate business tasks with AI agents across 400+ apps. License: Sustainable Use. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free self-hosted Community Edition (fair-code license). The catch: SSO, Git version control and Projects are not in the free Community Edition; they need a paid Business or Enterprise plan (works with local AI)
- [Activepieces](https://openorbia.com/tool/activepieces/): No-code automation with AI steps and agents. License: MIT core. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free self-hosted (MIT core); free cloud plan with 1,000 credits/mo. The catch: SSO is on the paid Team plan; audit logs, Git sync and custom roles are on the enterprise plan
- [Open WebUI](https://openorbia.com/tool/open-webui/): Self-hosted chat interface for local or cloud AI models. Works with Ollama. License: Open WebUI License. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Self-hosted; Open WebUI License with a branding clause. The catch: Has no models of its own: connect Ollama or an API. Removing branding needs permission or a license once users pass 50. (works with local AI)
- [Dify](https://openorbia.com/tool/dify/): Build an AI support chatbot on your own docs and embed it on your site. License: Dify License. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free self-hosted Community Edition; free cloud Sandbox (200 credits). The catch: License: no multi-workspace service without written permission from Dify, and the logo and copyright must stay (works with local AI)
- [Meetily](https://openorbia.com/tool/meetily/): Records, transcribes and summarizes meetings on your own laptop. License: MIT. Setup: Desktop app. Free tier: Free desktop app (MIT Community Edition); paid PRO separate. The catch: Speaker identification, integrations and advanced exports are in paid PRO; Ollama is the recommended local option for summaries (works with local AI)
- [Postiz](https://openorbia.com/tool/postiz/): Schedule social media posts and write them with AI. License: AGPL-3.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (AGPL); paid cloud with 7-day trial. The catch: Self-hosting means registering your own developer app on each social network; some, like Meta and TikTok, need app review
- [Inbox Zero](https://openorbia.com/tool/inbox-zero/): AI email assistant that sorts your inbox and drafts replies. License: AGPL-3.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (AGPL). The catch: Self-hosting needs your own Google OAuth app (Microsoft is optional); AI can run on Ollama (free) or your own key
- [paperless-gpt](https://openorbia.com/tool/paperless-gpt/): AI reads, tags and files your scanned receipts and invoices. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free and open source when self-hosted (MIT). The catch: Needs an existing paperless-ngx install plus an OpenAI key or Ollama (works with local AI)
- [Vane](https://openorbia.com/tool/vane/): Self-hosted AI search with cited sources. Formerly Perplexica. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free and open source when self-hosted (MIT). The catch: Needs your own AI API key or a local model via Ollama (works with local AI)
- [LibreChat](https://openorbia.com/tool/librechat/): Self-hosted chat app for many AI models, with user accounts. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Open source (MIT license); you host it yourself. The catch: Needs your own AI API keys, or a local model via Ollama (works with local AI)
- [RAGFlow](https://openorbia.com/tool/ragflow/): Ask questions across large piles of PDFs, contracts and manuals. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (Apache-2.0). The catch: Recommends 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM and 50 GB disk; models can run locally with Ollama or vLLM, or use your own key (works with local AI)
- [Jan](https://openorbia.com/tool/jan/): Offline desktop app for chatting with local AI models License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Desktop app. Free tier: Free desktop app with offline local models. The catch: Needs 8 GB RAM minimum (16 GB recommended); cloud models need your own API key from that provider (works with local AI)
- [Open Notebook](https://openorbia.com/tool/open-notebook/): Private, self-hosted NotebookLM alternative: chat with your documents, PDFs and web pages. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free & open source (MIT); you pay only for a cloud AI if you use one. The catch: Needs Docker. No password by default: bind it to 127.0.0.1 or set one. Podcasts need a text-to-speech provider; Ollama has none (works with local AI)
- [Langflow](https://openorbia.com/tool/langflow/): Build AI agents and automated workflows visually, then run them as an API or MCP server. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free & open source (MIT); you pay only for a cloud AI model you connect. The catch: Needs Python 3.10-3.14 and uv, or Docker. Local models need Ollama and enough memory. The Desktop app download asks for your email (works with local AI)

## Job seekers

- [career-ops](https://openorbia.com/tool/career-ops/): AI agent that scans job boards, scores your fit, tailors your CV and letters, and tracks your pipeline. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free (MIT); runs inside an AI coding CLI on your machine. The catch: Free AI tiers (Gemini, OpenRouter) are rate limited; local Ollama needs suitable hardware and larger models for reliable results (works with local AI)
- [Resume Matcher](https://openorbia.com/tool/resume-matcher/): Scores your resume against a job post, then tailors it and drafts a cover letter. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (Apache-2.0). The catch: You pick the model: local Ollama, your coding agent, or your own cloud API key (works with local AI)
- [Reactive Resume](https://openorbia.com/tool/reactive-resume/): Open-source resume builder with optional AI writing help. License: MIT. Setup: Browser, ready to use. Free tier: All resume features free at rxresu.me; MIT self-host too. The catch: AI writing help needs your own key or Ollama
- [JobSync](https://openorbia.com/tool/jobsync/): Self-hosted job application tracker with AI resume review and fit scoring. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (MIT). The catch: Docker setup; AI uses Ollama by default, or your own cloud key (works with local AI)
- [JobOps](https://openorbia.com/tool/jobops/): Self-hosted job search pipeline: find jobs, AI-score them 0–100, tailor your resume. License: AGPL + Commons Clause. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted; hosted cloud is paid. The catch: Includes anonymous usage analytics (opt out by blocking umami.dakheera47.com); Commons Clause: no selling or paid hosting (works with local AI)
- [DeepInterview](https://openorbia.com/tool/deepinterview/): Voice AI mock interviewer built from your CV and the job description. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (Apache-2.0). The catch: Live voice needs LiveKit plus speech and AI keys, or a fully local setup (works with local AI)
- [ResuLLMe](https://openorbia.com/tool/resullme/): Rewrites and enhances your resume with AI. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (MIT); public demo available. The catch: Needs an OpenAI or Gemini key, or a self-hosted model such as Ollama (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- [MyResumo](https://openorbia.com/tool/myresumo/): Tailors your resume and skills to a specific job description. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (MIT). The catch: Needs an AI API key (DeepSeek by default, or OpenAI) and a MongoDB database
- [GrillKit](https://openorbia.com/tool/grillkit/): Self-hosted voice trainer for technical interviews with real-time scoring. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted (Apache-2.0). The catch: Bring your own model: Ollama/vLLM locally or a cloud API key (works with local AI)
- [Interview Coach](https://openorbia.com/tool/interview-coach/): Voice interview simulator with command-line and web modes. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free command-line tool with a local web dashboard. The catch: Use Ollama for offline use, or a cloud AI provider (works with local AI)
- [ElevateLI](https://openorbia.com/tool/elevateli/): Chrome extension that scores your LinkedIn profile and suggests AI improvements. License: MIT. Setup: Desktop app. Free tier: MIT-licensed Chrome extension, no account; AI use billed by your provider. The catch: Not on the Chrome Web Store (load unpacked); AI needs your own key or Ollama (works with local AI)
- [JobSync-Service](https://openorbia.com/tool/jobsync-service/): Finds jobs straight from company hiring systems (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby) for your AI assistant. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free code (MIT); you deploy it yourself. The catch: Needs an AI app that supports MCP (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor); that app's plan limits apply
- [Abhyas](https://openorbia.com/tool/abhyas/): Voice mock interview based on your resume and the job description. License: MIT. Setup: Browser, ready to use. Free tier: Free (MIT); runs in your browser, data stays on your device. The catch: Voice needs your own Gemini/OpenAI key; local models are text-only (works with local AI)
- [ai-job-search](https://openorbia.com/tool/ai-job-search/): Turns Claude Code into a job search assistant: search, scoring, CV and interview prep. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free framework (MIT) you fork and run locally. The catch: Needs a paid Claude plan or API credits
- [AI Job Hunter](https://openorbia.com/tool/ai-job-hunter/): Desktop app that finds jobs, scores them against your résumé and writes tailored cover letters and résumés License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Desktop app. Free tier: Free and open source; runs offline with Ollama or uses your own API key. The catch: Large, fast-changing app; crash reports go to Sentry by default (can turn off) (works with local AI)

## Security teams

- [garak](https://openorbia.com/tool/garak/): Scans AI chatbots and LLM apps for jailbreaks, prompt injection and data leaks. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free command-line scanner (Apache-2.0). The catch: Needs a target model to test: a local Hugging Face model, or an API (OpenAI, Cohere, Groq and others) with your own key (works with local AI)
- [promptfoo](https://openorbia.com/tool/promptfoo/): Tests and red-teams AI apps, agents and RAG for vulnerabilities. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free CLI (MIT); red teaming capped at 10k probes/month. The catch: Red-team generation uses promptfoo's servers unless you set your own key or model (works with local AI)
- [PyRIT](https://openorbia.com/tool/pyrit/): Microsoft's open framework for red-teaming generative AI systems. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free Python library (MIT). The catch: You configure your own AI endpoints and keys
- [Tracecat](https://openorbia.com/tool/tracecat/): Security automation (SOAR) platform built around AI agents for SOC teams. License: AGPL-3.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free self-hosted (AGPL): 1 workspace, unlimited workflows. The catch: Free plan includes SSO and audit logs; REST API, Git sync, forms and metrics need the paid Team plan (works with local AI)
- [Strix](https://openorbia.com/tool/strix/): AI agents that find and confirm vulnerabilities in your apps. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free command-line tool (Apache-2.0). The catch: Needs Docker plus an AI key or local model; authorized testing only (works with local AI)
- [PentestGPT](https://openorbia.com/tool/pentestgpt/): AI penetration testing assistant from published security research. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free (MIT); run locally or in Docker. The catch: Main mode needs a Claude Code/Codex login; Ollama only in legacy mode (works with local AI)
- [PentAGI](https://openorbia.com/tool/pentagi/): Self-hosted multi-agent system for automated pentests on systems you are authorized to test. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted with Docker (MIT). The catch: Needs an LLM (cloud key or local Ollama/vLLM); a EULA applies; only test systems you own or are authorized to assess (works with local AI)
- [NeMo Guardrails](https://openorbia.com/tool/nemo-guardrails/): Add programmable safety rules to AI chatbots. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free Python library (Apache-2.0). The catch: Collects anonymous usage telemetry (opt out with DO_NOT_TRACK=1); you choose and configure the LLM it guards (works with local AI)
- [Vigil](https://openorbia.com/tool/vigil/): AI SOC platform for alert triage and investigation with your own LLM. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free when self-hosted with Docker (Apache-2.0). The catch: Runs several Docker services (PostgreSQL, Redis, Bifrost); AI needs your own provider key or local Ollama (works with local AI)
- [Shannon](https://openorbia.com/tool/shannon/): AI agent that pentests web apps and APIs. License: AGPL-3.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free CLI (AGPL); you pay only your own AI costs. The catch: Needs your source code and an AI key; black-box testing is paid Pro (works with local AI)
- [PurpleLlama](https://openorbia.com/tool/purplellama/): Meta's AI safety models, prompt-injection detection and security benchmarks. License: Llama Community License. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Evals and CodeShield: MIT. Llama Guard, Prompt Guard: Llama Community licenses. The catch: Benchmarks test an LLM you supply, through a provider API key or a self-hosted model (works with local AI)
- [AiSOC](https://openorbia.com/tool/aisoc/): Self-hosted AI SOC: alert merging, AI triage and MITRE ATT&CK investigations. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Open source and self-hostable (MIT); runs without an API key. The catch: Needs Docker Compose with 8 GB memory; the bundled local AI model is small, not a frontier model (works with local AI)
- [HexStrike AI](https://openorbia.com/tool/hexstrike-ai/): Connects AI agents to 150+ existing security tools through MCP. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free MCP server (MIT). The catch: Needs an MCP AI app and the security tools installed; some optional tools are paid; run in an isolated VM on systems you're authorized to test
- [SOC Range](https://openorbia.com/tool/soc-range/): SOC analyst training simulator with an optional local AI Triage Copilot: alert summaries, MITRE ATT&CK mapping and next steps. License: MIT. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free (MIT); runs locally with Node.js or Docker. The catch: Simulated data only; the optional AI Copilot needs local Ollama (works with local AI, built by OpenOrbia's founder)
- [Nebula](https://openorbia.com/tool/nebula/): AI assistant for pentest operators. Works with local models. License: BSD-2-Clause. Setup: Desktop app. Free tier: Free desktop app (BSD-2). The catch: Linux x86_64 preview installers only (DEB or AppImage); needs your own model (Ollama, vLLM, Claude, OpenRouter); voice incurs OpenAI charges (works with local AI)
- [Agentic Security](https://openorbia.com/tool/agentic-security/): Scan your AI app or LLM endpoint with jailbreak and prompt-injection test datasets. License: Apache-2.0. Setup: Install & self-host. Free tier: Free & open source (Apache 2.0); no SaaS, no account. The catch: Needs Python 3.15+. Scanning a paid API costs one call per prompt; test datasets download from Hugging Face (works with local AI)

- [Self-hosted AI tools](https://openorbia.com/collection/self-hosted/): tools you run on your own server or computer
- [Free AI APIs](https://openorbia.com/free-ai-apis/): free tiers of AI model APIs, checked against each provider's own pages
- [This week's launches](https://openorbia.com/launches/): Launch Week, new tools every Monday
